Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 4 th Of September, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 1093 of 2022
 Smt. Shantibai And Others
 Versus
 Kanhaiyalal And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Jahangir M. Poonegar, learned counsel for the a
 Shri Sudhir Dandwate, learned counsel for the respon
 Order
The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 2.9.2021 passed in Claim Case No.3806/2018 challenging the quantum of compensation.
The liability of the Insurance Company is not under dispute.
2. Short facts of the case are that on 31.10.2018 at around 4.00 in the evening deceased Bharat Singh was going by his motorcycle from Panchrundi to his village Chhota Ranipada.
When he reached near Chhapan Phata, Lilikhedi, Truck No.RJ-06-JB-4562 came from behind, which was being driven by its driver in rash and negligent manner, dashed into the motorcycle of deceased.
Because of which he sustained grievous injuries and resultantly died on the spot.
2.1 The claimants-appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act claiming compensation for his death.

The claims NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25172 2 MA-1093-2022 Tribunal after considering the evidence available on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,74,500/- to the appellants out of which an amount of Rs.8,77,500/- was for loss of dependency.
3. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the claims Tribunal has erred in calculating the loss of dependency for the reason of incorrect assessment of income of the deceased.
He points out that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month by running a business of selling milk and from agricultural work.
He further submits that in any case income of the deceased could not have been taken below Rs.7,325/- per month as that was the minimum wages for unskilled Labour at the relevant time.
However, the claims Tribunal has taken income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month, which is not sustainable in view of the facts of the case.
He, thus prays for enhancement of the compensation.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/Insurance company points out that the claims Tribunal in para 18 of the impugned award has considered the claim of income and after recording findings that there was no material available on record to establish that the deceased was earning Rs.15,000/- per month.
Therefore, the claims Tribunal has taken income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month.
Hence, there is no illegality in the findings recorded by the claims Tribunal.
He, thus prays for dismissal of the appeal.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.

6. The findings as recorded by the claims Tribunal in para 18 are found to be correct to the extent that there is no material whatsoever for NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:25172 3 MA-1093-2022 establishing income of the deceased at Rs.15,000/- per month.
As such to that extent no interference is warranted.

However, on perusal of the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority this Court thinks it proper that it is correct that the minimum wages at the relevant time for unskilled Labour were Rs.7,325/- per month.
As such, the same is taken as income of the deceased at the time of accident.

Apart from this, all other aspects of the award are found to be in accordance with law and after quantifying the compensation in view of the changed income of the deceased the compensation for loss of dependency would come to Rs.10,71,278/- and after deducting the amount already awarded under such head the amount now comes to Rs.1,93,778/-.
This amount shall be paid over and above the amount already awarded by the claims Tribunal.

The enhanced amount shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim application till its payment.
7. With the above, the present Misc.Appeal stands disposed off.

( PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE patil Smt. Shantibai vs Kanhaiyalal on 4 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/79503691/
